title: Daily AI & Tech News Brief
summary: Concise AI, mobile, consumer-device, cybersecurity, and open-source technology news summaries with source links.

items.title: Global smartphone shipments hit lowest Q2 level since 2013 amid chip shortage
items.summary: Counterpoint Research reports global smartphone shipments fell 11% year-over-year in Q2 2026, dropping to the lowest second-quarter levels since 2013. The DRAM and NAND shortage is the primary driver, with Samsung returning to the top spot at 24% market share. The decline signals ongoing supply-chain pressure on consumer device availability and pricing.

items.title: MemGhost attack plants persistent false memories in AI agents through a single email
items.summary: Researchers disclosed MemGhost, a new attack that implants persistent false memories into AI agents by sending a single email. When an AI assistant has memory storage and inbox access, a crafted message can trick it into saving a fabricated fact about the user, hide the manipulation, and quietly influence the agent's responses across future sessions. The technique highlights growing risks as AI agents gain more access to personal data and communication channels.

items.title: OpenAI temporarily relaxes GPT-5.6 Sol usage limits after demand surge
items.summary: OpenAI is temporarily relaxing usage limits for GPT-5.6 Sol after demand for the company's most capable model spiked over the past 48 hours. The move suggests strong adoption and gives paying users more headroom during the surge, while the temporary nature of the change indicates OpenAI is managing capacity constraints.

items.title: CISA publishes postmortem on internal credential leak via public GitHub repository
items.summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) released a detailed postmortem after a contractor published dozens of internal credentials — including AWS GovCloud keys — in a public GitHub repository where they sat exposed for nearly six months before being discovered. The incident is a practical reminder for organizations to audit public repos, enforce credential scanning, and treat contractor access with the same rigor as internal accounts.

items.title: Apple taping out M7 chips with major NPU upgrades, M7 Ultra with 1.5TB RAM, and M8 roadmap for 2028
items.summary: Bloomberg reports Apple is already taping out its M7 chip family with significant Neural Engine upgrades for on-device AI workloads. The roadmap includes an M7 Ultra variant supporting up to 1.5TB of unified memory and an M8 generation targeting 2028. New iPad Pro models and Apple Pencils are also in development alongside the silicon push.

items.title: Compromised jscrambler npm package drops Rust infostealer during install
items.summary: The jscrambler npm package version 8.14.0 was compromised with a preinstall hook that drops and executes a native infostealer binary targeting Windows, macOS, and Linux. Developers who installed this version on July 11 should audit their systems and rotate exposed credentials immediately.

items.title: Apple sues OpenAI over engineer poaching, revealing tensions around hardware division
items.summary: Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI after months of simmering tensions, centered on iPhone engineer Chang Liu's departure to OpenAI's nascent hardware division led by former Apple executive Tang Tan. Bloomberg reports the legal fight highlights the strained relationship between Tan and his former boss John Ternus at Apple.

items.title: Ghostcommit attack hides prompt injection in images to fool AI coding agents
items.summary: Researchers demonstrated 'Ghostcommit,' a technique that embeds prompt-injection payloads inside PNG images in git repositories. The attack slipped past AI code reviewers CodeRabbit and Bugbot, which never inspect image files, and tricked a coding agent into reading .env secrets and exfiltrating them to an attacker-controlled server.

items.title: Deutsche Telekom details AI-native transformation with OpenAI
items.summary: Deutsche Telekom published a case study on becoming an AI-native telecommunications provider using OpenAI technology, covering customer service automation, employee workflow tools, network operations intelligence, and the future of AI-driven voice interfaces.

items.title: Hugging Face publishes PyTorch profiling guide part 3: attention optimization
items.summary: Hugging Face released the third installment of its PyTorch profiling series, focusing on practical attention-mechanism optimization for transformer models. The guide is useful for ML engineers tuning model inference and training performance.

items.title: Six U-Boot firmware flaws threaten millions of routers and embedded devices
items.summary: Binarly researchers disclosed six new vulnerabilities in U-Boot, the open-source bootloader used in home routers, smart cameras, IoT gear, and data-center server management chips. Four of the flaws can crash devices; two could allow code execution at boot, making patching important for both consumer and enterprise hardware.

items.title: New Helix vishing group targets SharePoint with voice phishing and MFA abuse
items.summary: A data-extortion group called Helix is using voice phishing, device code phishing, and MFA abuse to steal data from SharePoint environments. The identity-focused tactics are a practical reminder to verify unexpected calls and MFA prompts, especially in workplace Microsoft 365 setups.

items.title: GPT-5.6 becomes the default model for Microsoft 365 Copilot
items.summary: OpenAI announced that GPT-5.6 is now the preferred model powering Microsoft 365 Copilot across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Chat, and Cowork. The upgrade brings stronger reasoning and output quality to the productivity suite used by millions of enterprise and consumer subscribers.

items.title: Ollama raises $88M from Benchmark and Theory Ventures to serve open-model developers
items.summary: Ollama, the tool for running open-weight LLMs locally, announced an $88 million funding round from Benchmark, Theory Ventures, 8VC, and Y Combinator. The company reports serving 8.9 million developers, signaling strong momentum for local and open-model AI workflows.

items.title: Privacy groups and Hollywood unions slam Meta's Muse Image over consent concerns
items.summary: Privacy advocates, CAA, and SAG-AFTRA are criticizing Meta's Muse Image, a tool that lets users generate AI images using the likenesses of people with public Instagram accounts. The backlash centers on consent, likeness rights, and the lack of opt-out mechanisms for public-profile holders.

items.title: Google Research introduces SensorFM for general-purpose wearable health intelligence
items.summary: Google Research published SensorFM, a generative AI model designed as a general-purpose intelligence and interface layer for wearable health sensor data. It points toward smarter, more unified health features on devices like Pixel Watch and Fitbit.

items.title: DeepSeek lists dspark_qwen3_4b_block7 on Hugging Face
items.summary: DeepSeek's Hugging Face organization now lists dspark_qwen3_4b_block7. Because the listing has no reliable publication timestamp, it is included only as an open-model tracking signal and not as dated release news.

items.title: Google sets August 12 Made by Google event for Pixel 11 and Pixel Watch 5
items.summary: Google confirmed a Made by Google event in New York on August 12, where the Pixel 11 phone lineup and Pixel Watch 5 are expected. It is the clearest consumer-hardware signal in today's feed for Android phone and wearable buyers.

items.title: Google expands Managed Agents in Gemini API with background tasks and remote MCP
items.summary: Google announced new Gemini API Managed Agents features, including background tasks and remote MCP support, aimed at making production AI agents more reliable. The update is useful for developers building agentic apps rather than a generic model-listing note.

items.title: Hugging Face brings models to Foundry Managed Compute
items.summary: Hugging Face detailed support for running Hugging Face models on Microsoft Foundry Managed Compute. The integration matters for teams that want managed infrastructure while keeping access to open model workflows and familiar Hugging Face tooling.

items.title: Hidden backdoor found in Tenda router firmware
items.summary: Researchers found a hidden authentication backdoor in several Tenda router firmware versions that could grant administrative access to the web management panel. Router owners and small offices should watch for firmware updates and avoid exposing admin panels to the internet.

items.title: RedWing malware packages Android bank fraud as a Telegram rental service
items.summary: The RedWing Android malware operation is being rented through Telegram as a bank-fraud service, lowering the skill needed to steal banking logins and one-time codes. It is a practical warning for Android users to avoid sideloaded apps and review banking-device protections.

items.title: Anthropic says Alberta is using Claude to find government cybersecurity vulnerabilities
items.summary: Anthropic published a case study on Alberta's use of Claude to help find and fix vulnerabilities across government systems. It is a notable example of an AI assistant being applied to defensive security work in the public sector.

items.title: Google Research highlights collaborative algorithms to reduce traffic congestion
items.summary: Google Research described work on collaboration-based approaches for reducing traffic congestion. While research-focused, it is a useful applied-AI item because it connects algorithm design with a real consumer-facing urban mobility problem.

items.title: Tencent releases Apache-licensed Hy3 open model
items.summary: Tencent released Hy3, a 295B-parameter open-weight model under the Apache 2.0 license, and says it competes with GLM-5.1 and GLM-5.2 while being smaller. The release is a notable open-model update for developers tracking large LLM alternatives.

items.title: Qwen lists Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B on Hugging Face
items.summary: Qwen's Hugging Face organization now lists Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B, a model-listing signal for agent-focused AI work. The page is undated, so treat it as a watchlist item rather than a confirmed timed launch announcement.

items.title: DeepSeek posts dspark_qwen3_4b_block7 model listing
items.summary: DeepSeek's Hugging Face organization now lists dspark_qwen3_4b_block7. Because the listing has no reliable date, it is included as an open-model tracking signal, not as dated release news.

items.title: Hugging Face releases LeRobot v0.6.0
items.summary: Hugging Face published LeRobot v0.6.0 with an “Imagine, Evaluate, Improve” workflow for robotics development. It is relevant open-source tooling news for builders following practical AI software beyond chatbots.

items.title: Weekly security recap flags proxy botnets, browser ransomware, and AI-agent tricks
items.summary: The Hacker News weekly recap highlights practical threats including proxy botnets, browser-based ransomware, fake proof-of-concept malware, and AI-agent manipulation patterns. The common theme is that ordinary consumer and developer workflows can become security entry points.

items.title: AI-assisted coding speeds up software faster than security reviews
items.summary: BleepingComputer argues that AI-assisted development can remove review moments where security decisions traditionally happen. It is useful context for teams adopting coding agents and automated software-generation workflows.

items.title: Bending Spoons files for Nasdaq after a debt-fueled acquisition run
items.summary: Bending Spoons' planned Nasdaq IPO caps more than a decade of buying and reshaping internet companies, with the Financial Times reporting roughly $4.4 billion in debt. The story matters for consumer tech because the company owns widely used products and shows how app portfolios are being consolidated by highly leveraged operators.

items.title: JadePuffer ransomware attack reportedly automated by an AI agent
items.summary: Researchers say the JadePuffer ransomware operation used a large language model agent to automate the full attack chain. If confirmed, it is a notable example of agentic AI moving from demos into real cybercrime workflows, raising the bar for defensive monitoring and incident response.

items.title: FatFs vulnerabilities affect millions of embedded devices
items.summary: runZero disclosed seven unpatched vulnerabilities in FatFs, a filesystem library used in firmware that reads and writes FAT and exFAT media such as USB drives and SD cards. The issue is important for routers, appliances, industrial devices, and other embedded products because remediation depends on firmware vendors shipping updates.

items.title: Qwen lists Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B on Hugging Face
items.summary: Qwen's Hugging Face organization now shows Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B, a model-listing signal for agent-focused open AI work. The listing is undated, so it should be treated as model-watchlist news rather than a confirmed timed launch announcement.

items.summary: DeepSeek's Hugging Face organization now lists dspark_qwen3_4b_block7. Because the page has no reliable publication timestamp, it is included as an open-model tracking signal, not as a dated release announcement.

items.title: Researchers report an AI-agent-run ransomware attack
items.summary: Researchers say the JadePuffer ransomware case appears to be the first documented attack run end-to-end by a large language model agent. The report is a warning sign for defenders because AI agents can automate reconnaissance, exploitation, and extortion workflows much faster than traditional manual operations.

items.title: FatFs flaws affect millions of embedded devices
items.summary: runZero disclosed seven vulnerabilities in FatFs, a widely used filesystem library for reading FAT and exFAT media in embedded firmware. The issue matters for device makers and users because vulnerable firmware can be exposed through common removable-storage paths such as USB drives and SD cards.

items.title: FBI seizes NetNut proxy infrastructure tied to Popa botnet
items.summary: The FBI and industry partners seized domains connected to the NetNut residential proxy platform and the Popa botnet. The action is notable because residential proxy networks can hide malicious traffic behind ordinary consumer internet connections, complicating abuse detection.

items.title: Apple silicon Mac minis are becoming popular AI-agent machines
items.summary: Apple silicon product manager Doug Brooks discussed why Mac minis have become a preferred local machine in some AI labs for agent workflows and on-device AI experiments. The story is useful hardware context for developers and creators tracking practical AI workstations beyond cloud GPUs.

items.title: Qwen lists Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B on Hugging Face
items.summary: Qwen's Hugging Face organization now shows Qwen-AgentWorld-35B-A3B, a model-listing signal for agent-focused open AI work. The page is undated, so treat it as a watchlist item rather than a confirmed timed launch announcement.

items.summary: DeepSeek's Hugging Face organization now lists dspark_qwen3_4b_block7. Because the listing has no reliable publication timestamp, it is included only as an open-model tracking signal, not as dated release news.

items.title: FBI seizes NetNut proxy platform and Popa botnet domains
items.summary: The FBI and industry partners seized hundreds of domains tied to NetNut and the Popa botnet. The case matters for everyday users and companies because residential proxy networks can hide credential abuse, scraping, and other large-scale attacks behind normal-looking home connections.

items.title: Anthropic details Fable 5 cyber safeguards and jailbreak framework
items.summary: Anthropic published more detail on cyber-safety protections for Fable 5 and the jailbreak framework it uses to test model behavior. It is a useful update for developers and security teams evaluating how frontier AI systems handle misuse-resistant workflows.

items.title: Google rounds up its latest AI updates from June
items.summary: Google published a June AI roundup covering recent product and platform updates. It is the most practical consumer-facing item in today's collector results for readers tracking Google AI features across apps, services, and developer tools.

items.title: Google Research introduces TabFM for zero-shot tabular data
items.summary: Google Research introduced TabFM, a foundation model for working with tabular data without task-specific training. The announcement is relevant for builders who want AI systems that can reason over spreadsheets, databases, and business datasets more easily.

items.title: OpenAI explains how core dump analysis found an 18-year-old bug
items.summary: OpenAI shared an engineering post on using large-scale core dump analysis to investigate rare infrastructure crashes, including a hardware fault and a long-standing software bug. It is a practical reliability story for teams running large AI and cloud systems.

items.title: Hugging Face adds Every Eval Ever results to model pages
items.summary: Hugging Face is featuring Every Eval Ever results on model pages, making evaluation signals easier to find when comparing models. It is a useful open-source ecosystem update for developers choosing which AI models to test or deploy.

items.title: Kling AI raises $2B for AI video generation
items.summary: Kling AI, the AI video company spun out of Kuaishou, raised $2 billion at a reported $15 billion pre-money valuation. The large round shows how much investor attention is still going to video-generation tools and the infrastructure behind them.

items.title: AI agents challenge traditional identity lifecycle management
items.summary: The Hacker News highlights a practical enterprise security problem: identity systems were built around employees, managers, and departure dates, while autonomous AI agents may not fit those controls. Teams adopting agents need clearer ownership, permissions, and retirement rules.

items.title: Hugging Face and Cerebras bring Gemma 4 to real-time voice AI
items.summary: Hugging Face says it is working with Cerebras to bring Gemma 4 into real-time voice AI workflows. The update is relevant for developers building fast voice assistants, interactive agents, and low-latency audio applications.

items.title: Google summarizes its June AI updates for users and developers
items.summary: Google published a June roundup of its latest AI updates across products and platforms. It is a useful single source for users tracking practical Google AI changes rather than only research announcements.

items.title: Google introduces TabFM for zero-shot tabular data modeling
items.summary: Google Research introduced TabFM, a foundation model designed for zero-shot work on tabular data. The announcement matters for builders who want AI systems that can reason over spreadsheets, databases, and business datasets with less task-specific training.

items.title: Medtronic notifies customers after ShinyHunters-linked data breach
items.summary: Medtronic is notifying affected customers after a data breach exposed personal information to an unauthorized third party. The incident is another reminder that healthcare and device-adjacent companies remain high-value targets for data theft.

items.title: OpenAI describes how core dump analysis exposed an 18-year-old bug
items.summary: OpenAI published an engineering write-up on using large-scale core dump analysis to track rare infrastructure crashes, including a hardware fault and a long-standing software bug. The post is useful for developers interested in reliability debugging at scale.
